BiblicalUsage: Beel is the Aramaic word for master, lord, a title of authority. It is the word for Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe who write their accusation against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes, and for the king's answer that is sent back to them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the masters of this world write their letters and the King of heaven writes His answer, because Rehum's accusation stops the building for a season and God's decree restarts it. The chancellor's title is real and his power is temporary, and I hold that no letter from a master on earth can overrule the decree of the Master in heaven.
